The AI market is heading for a mass extinction event.

Gartner's chief forecaster went on CNBC this week and delivered a stark prediction: every AI market they track will collapse into a duopoly. Two dominant players per category. Everyone else gets acquired or shut down.

The trigger is simple math. Compute capacity has already outpaced demand. AI companies are burning through billions giving away tokens through freemium tiers, racing to be the last one standing. OpenAI itself just cut its own revenue forecast by $50 billion — while raising another $30 billion at a $1.3 trillion valuation.

For business leaders, this is not an abstract market story. This is vendor risk. The AI providers you are building on today may merge, pivot, or vanish. The infrastructure layer you chose six months ago may belong to a competitor next year.

The companies that survive the shakeout will control pricing for the next decade of enterprise AI. The window to build modular, portable AI architectures — with real exit clauses — is closing fast.
